questions.stem: At a medical-surveillance planning meeting, a supervisor proposes: "The symptomatic employee must have fabricated the response because the air results were similar". The underlying case is: Two employees perform the same task with similar measured airborne exposure, but one develops symptoms at a much lower cumulative dose. Which explanation is most scientifically defensible? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Individual susceptibility, health status, route, metabolism, and other modifiers can change the response at a similar measured exposure
A dose-response relationship requires every exposed person to experience identical effects
The symptomatic employee must have fabricated the response because the air results were similar
Base the toxicological judgment on concentration alone and exclude exposure duration and host susceptibility
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Dose-response relationships describe patterns, not identical outcomes for every person. Host factors and exposure characteristics can materially alter absorbed dose and response.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'A dose-response relationship requires every exposed person to experience identical effects' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling dose-response and susceptibility principle.

The proposed response 'The symptomatic employee must have fabricated the response because the air results were similar' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling dose-response and susceptibility principle.

The proposed response 'Base the toxicological judgment on concentration alone and exclude exposure duration and host susceptibility' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling dose-response and susceptibility principle.

questions.stem: At a chemical substitution review, a supervisor proposes: "Injection only, unless the liquid is heated above its boiling point". The underlying case is: A corrosive liquid has low volatility but is handled manually with frequent splashing. Which exposure route deserves the greatest immediate control emphasis? Skin and eye contact, while still evaluating inhalation generated by mist or aerosol
Injection only, unless the liquid is heated above its boiling point
Inhalation only, because workplace chemicals enter the body exclusively through the lungs
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Low volatility does not eliminate dermal and ocular hazards. Splashing makes contact a primary concern, while aerosol generation can still create inhalation exposure.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Ingestion only, because liquids cannot penetrate or damage skin' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling route of entry principle.
The proposed response 'Injection only, unless the liquid is heated above its boiling point' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling route of entry principle.
The proposed response 'Inhalation only, because workplace chemicals enter the body exclusively through the lungs' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling route of entry principle.

questions.stem: At an exposure-route assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Only the immediate effect matters because chronic outcomes are not occupational". The underlying case is: A substance can cause immediate central nervous system depression at high concentration and liver injury after repeated lower exposures. How should these effects be characterized? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Only the chronic effect matters because acute symptoms resolve quickly
The two effects cancel each other when exposure is below the flammable limit
The substance has both acute and chronic toxic effects that require controls addressing peak and cumulative exposure
Only the immediate effect matters because chronic outcomes are not occupational
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A chemical can produce different acute and chronic endpoints. Effective risk management considers short-term peaks and long-term cumulative dose independently of flammability.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Only the chronic effect matters because acute symptoms resolve quickly' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling acute versus chronic toxicity principle.
The proposed response 'The two effects cancel each other when exposure is below the flammable limit' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling acute versus chronic toxicity principle.
The proposed response 'Only the immediate effect matters because chronic outcomes are not occupational' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling acute versus chronic toxicity principle.

questions.stem: At an acute illness investigation, a supervisor proposes: "Bioaccumulation of an inert gas in bone tissue". The underlying case is: An employee previously exposed without symptoms now develops asthma-like reactions at very low concentrations of an isocyanate. questions.stem: At a chronic exposure assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Exclude all employees of childbearing age from the job regardless of exposure level". The underlying case is: A process uses a chemical associated with developmental toxicity. Management proposes protecting only pregnant employees after they disclose pregnancy. Control exposure for all potentially affected workers and use a nondiscriminatory program based on hazard and exposure, not pregnancy status alone
Wait for a confirmed pregnancy before evaluating engineering controls
Exclude all employees of childbearing age from the job regardless of exposure level

questions.stem: At an SDS toxicology review, a supervisor proposes: "Carcinogenicity is irrelevant whenever no acute symptoms are reported". The underlying case is: A manager argues that a low measured concentration proves a known occupational carcinogen presents zero risk. Which response is most appropriate? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Only odor threshold is needed to determine carcinogenic risk
Carcinogenicity is irrelevant whenever no acute symptoms are reported
A low concentration may reduce risk, but risk characterization must consider potency, duration, uncertainty, applicable limits, and feasible exposure reduction
Treat any analytically detectable concentration as proof that every exposed worker will eventually develop cancer
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Carcinogenic risk is not established or excluded by one low result. Exposure magnitude, duration, evidence quality, standards, and control feasibility must be evaluated together.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Only odor threshold is needed to determine carcinogenic risk' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling carcinogen risk principle.
The proposed response 'Carcinogenicity is irrelevant whenever no acute symptoms are reported' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling carcinogen risk principle.

The proposed response 'Treat any analytically detectable concentration as proof that every exposed worker will eventually develop cancer' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling carcinogen risk principle.
